title: src/models/: how the order-2 model's counts adapt (a rate that slows as evidence grows)
context: One idea: how the order-2 model's count adapts. Today each count of 16 bits moves a sixteenth of the way towards each bit (RATE 4), whatever it has seen. Let it adapt faster while a context is new and slower as evidence grows (a small counter kept with the count), or keep two speeds at once and give both as predictions. Work in the order-2 file of src/models/ (new, predict, update). The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Today the total is 4,890,484 bytes, the message 3,544,012 and the program 1,346,472; a count's extra state must not cost more memory than the bound allows. The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/models/: a match model, the byte that followed the longest earlier match of the last bytes
context: Add a match model in one new file of src/models/ (read an existing model there for what a model gives: OUTPUTS, new, predict, update). It keeps its own history of the bytes seen and an index from a hash of the last few bytes to the place they last occurred; while the bytes just coded still match that earlier place, it predicts the bit that followed there, with a confidence that grows with the length of the match, and says nothing when there is no match. The corpus repeats long passages (refrains, speeches, names), which a model of three or four bytes cannot see. It needs the order-4 task done first, so that its gain is measured against the models a mixer will have. The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement and counts bytes exactly: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least half of one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes at least 1. There is no noise: a candidate one byte short is refused, and one that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Read the totals from the tip's last accepted verdict (message_bytes, program_bytes); at the cut that planned this line the total was 4,255,404 bytes, the message 2,904,836 and the program 1,350,568. The history costs memory: the tip used 87 MB for the corpus of 10,000,000 bytes. The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/models/: a new model of order 6, hashed, in its own file
context: Add a model of order 6: the six bytes before, with the bits of the byte known so far, choosing one count, hashed into a table sized to what the corpus needs, with a few bits of check in each slot so that a collision is not taken for evidence (read the order-4 file of src/models/ for what a model gives: OUTPUTS, new, predict, update).
